solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Assets in busy London?

parts.note: busy means occupied, at work, hence working
London is the UK's capital city

explanation.surface: Someone asks what valuables are to be found in bustling London.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that London is only an example of a capital, and the busy one is at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Working capital is the liquid funds a business holds for day-to-day running, a kind of financial asset.

clue.text: Animal with a growth that looks horrible

definitions.text: Animal with a growth that looks horrible

parts.words: Animal with a growth that looks horrible
parts.note: describes an ugly wild pig with prominent warty lumps on its face

explanation.surface: An ugly beast with an unsightly lump.
explanation.walkthrough: The growth is a wart, and the ugly animal it belongs to is a kind of hog.
explanation.definitionFit: The warthog is an African wild pig with wart-like facial protuberances, famously unlovely.

clue.text: Abhorrent ghoul I suspect will get a title demanding respect

indicators.note: suspect, read as doubtful, means the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A horrible ghoul will supposedly be given a dignified honorific.
explanation.definitionFit: Right Honourable is the formal style of address for privy counsellors and senior peers.

clue.text: Ailments kill some but not all

indicators.note: but not all says only part of the run of letters is taken, dropping the outer ones

explanation.surface: Diseases carry off a few people, though not everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across kILL Some.
explanation.definitionFit: Ills are troubles or illnesses, a near synonym of ailments.

clue.text: Elton (as he was!) turns up full of skill in band

indicators.note: full of means the turned name holds the word for skill inside it
turns up, in a down clue, means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Elton John was born Reginald Dwight, known as Reg
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Elton John's former self flips over, brimming with talent in a pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: A garter is an elastic band worn round the leg to hold up a stocking.

clue.text: Palace issuing false alarm — bah!

indicators.note: false signals the letters are not in their genuine order

explanation.surface: A palace sets off a bogus alarm, met with a scornful bah.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the Moorish palace-fortress in Granada, Spain.

clue.text: Justification when leader's ignored sign

indicators.note: leader's ignored means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: vindication is justification, being shown to be right

explanation.surface: An excuse offered when the boss has been passed over is a clear signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An indication is a sign or pointer to something.

clue.text: Enjoyable life that bears much fruit

definitions.meaning: the idiom life is just ... means life is pleasant
literally, a dish laden with cherries holds a lot of fruit

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a carefree, pleasant life, and literally a dish full of fruit.

clue.text: As one chooses a material

parts.note: twill is a woven fabric with diagonal ribs

explanation.surface: Picking a fabric just as you like.
explanation.definitionFit: At will means whenever or however one wishes.

clue.text: Soldier, say, in wild rural parts

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for say sits within the jumbled letters
wild means the letters of rural are thrown into disorder

parts.note: say is EG, short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A soldier, for instance, out in the untamed countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' adds nothing but the picture of country districts; 'say' is the usual signal for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a professional soldier in a standing army, as opposed to a reservist or volunteer.

clue.text: I perform full of energy in shed, somewhere to escape to

indicators.note: in places the filled phrase inside the word for a shed

parts.note: a hut is a small shed

indicators.note: full of means the pronoun-and-verb pair holds the energy symbol within it

parts.note: to perform is to do
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone acts energetically in a garden shed, their private retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts E inside IDO to give IDEO, and 'in' then sets that inside HUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideout is a hiding place, a refuge where someone can lie low.

clue.text: Has ancient thing on head, front of head

parts.note: a hat is worn on the head

indicators.note: front of asks for the opening letter of the second head

explanation.surface: An old possessor wears a hat right on the front of the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'has, in archaic form'.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic third-person singular of the verb to have, familiar from the King James Bible.

clue.text: Nasty creatures endlessly by small room, one providing food

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for nasty creatures loses its last letter

parts.note: vermin are pests, nasty creatures
a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Pests are found beside a tiny room where someone supplies meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermicelli is a very thin pasta, a staple food.

clue.text: Retirement accommodation in which former quizmaster entertains journalist companion

indicators.note: entertains means the quizmaster's name takes the others in as guests, holding them inside

parts.note: Bamber Gascoigne hosted the British TV quiz University Challenge for decades
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: In a retirement home a one-time quiz host hosts a reporter friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedchamber is a bedroom, where one goes on retiring for the night.

clue.text: Crawl in small wood by lake

parts.note: a grove is a small group of trees
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Creeping through a little copse beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To grovel is to crawl abjectly, literally or in servile behaviour.

clue.text: Lots of fuel for the fire to make you appreciative?

definitions.text: Lots of fuel for the fire to make you appreciative?

parts.words: Lots of fuel for the fire to make you appreciative?
parts.note: a fireplace grate that is full of fuel would make you thankful on a cold night, split as grate plus full

explanation.surface: A well-stocked fireplace would leave anyone thankful.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as GRATE FUL(L): a grate full of fuel; the spelling loses one L.
explanation.definitionFit: Grateful means thankful or appreciative, matching the clue's final word.

clue.text: With absence of duty, see number of people dying for nothing

parts.note: a death toll is the number killed
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: Tax-exempt, one sees the death count rise at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Duty here is a charge or levy, as on goods or a call.
explanation.definitionFit: Toll-free means without charge, with no fee or duty payable.

clue.text: Cut some meat quickly!

parts.note: to chop is to cut
a chop is a cut of meat, as a pork chop

explanation.surface: A butcher urging an apprentice to slice the meat fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop-chop is an informal exclamation meaning hurry up, at once.

clue.text: Collapse of once-famous Liverpool club, one not right

indicators.note: one not right means the letter for one stands where the right letter was

parts.note: the Cavern Club in Liverpool is where the Beatles played early on
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: The fall of a legendary Merseyside music venue, one not in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A cave-in is the falling in of a roof or mine, a collapse.

clue.text: Someone on an errand, it's said, for wood for Ark

indicators.note: it's said signals that the errand-runner's word is pronounced the same as the answer

parts.note: a gofer is a dogsbody who runs errands

explanation.surface: A runner sent on an errand to fetch timber for Noah's boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gopher wood is the material Noah used to build the ark in Genesis.

clue.text: Crumbling rubbish

explanation.definitionFit: Run-down means decaying; run down also means to belittle.

clue.text: Rabies may come from foreign country

indicators.note: may come from suggests a new word can be formed out of these letters

explanation.surface: A disease that might be brought in from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbia is a Balkan state, a country abroad to the British setter.

clue.text: Silver seal given special display in palace

indicators.note: special display suggests the letters are laid out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A silver seal is shown off at a royal palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Versailles is the great royal palace outside Paris built for Louis XIV.

clue.text: Press club

definitions.meaning: to press clothes is to smooth them with a hot appliance

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: smoothing laundry, and a metal-headed golf club.

clue.text: Cockney's pigeon gets some corn

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the initial aitch

parts.note: a homer is a homing pigeon

explanation.surface: A Londoner's bird pecks at a few grains.
explanation.definitionFit: An omer is an ancient Hebrew measure, also a sheaf of grain, hence a quantity of corn.

clue.text: I am sort of fish — little hesitation to be a drinker

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
the bib is a small fish of the cod family, also called pouting
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone admits to being a fish, then hesitates before confessing to drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink, so one who imbibes is a drinker.

clue.text: Small child's refusal to go to Disney film

indicators.note: to go to means the refusal is attached after the film title

parts.note: Bambi is the 1942 Disney animated film
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A toddler says no to being taken to see a Disney cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after child is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambino is Italian for a baby or young child, used informally in English.

clue.text: Member of group, nasty ogre, he being imprisoned in fortress

indicators.note: imprisoned in says the jumbled letters are locked inside the word for a fortress

parts.note: a garrison is a fortified military post

indicators.note: nasty signals that ogre and he are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unpleasant monster and a man are locked up in a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group' in the definition means a pop band, here the Beatles, not a set of things.
explanation.definitionFit: George Harrison was the lead guitarist of the Beatles, a member of that group.
